subject.declared_domain: The write path by which the incremental_updater Lambda materializes rows into the Iceberg table globgrph.graph_nodes via a Nessie-backed REST catalog. Covers the ONE atomic commit envelope in commit_batch() -- both of its exclusive branches (:501 overwrite for batches carrying upserts, :504 delete for delete-only batches). It does NOT cover this file's OTHER write path, the S3 branch-head marker (carded separately as W3-uuxp), and it does not cover the nightly full-derive (derive_runner.py, 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp~X's subjects) which writes the same table by a different mechanism.

methodology.how: SQS batch of CloudTrail management events -> extract changed ARNs -> bounded live AWS describe per ARN -> ONE pyiceberg commit into globgrph.graph_nodes. commit_batch() (:408) builds a SINGLE overwrite_filter spanning BOTH upsert keys and delete keys (:443), then applies exactly one of two exclusive branches: :501 table.overwrite(pa_table, overwrite_filter=combined_filter) when the batch carries nodes, or :504 table.delete(delete_filter=combined_filter) for a delete-only batch. Because overwrite = delete(filter) + append(rows), putting delete keys in the FILTER but not in the ROWS removes them in the same commit that refreshes the upserts. ⛔ I DELIBERATELY DO NOT SPLIT :501 AND :504 INTO TWO PATHS: same table, same bound (:434), same authority, same commit envelope, and the docstring at :412-424 states the single-envelope design explicitly. They are exclusive BRANCHES of one path, not two paths. The (FILE, WRITE PATH) grain distinguishes mechanism/bound/authority, and none of the three differs here.

declared_opinions: CORRECTNESS IS THE REF-CAS, NOT THE SNAPSHOT PARENT (:505-516). The code carries an explicit ruling that Nessie's branch-ref compare-and-swap is the off-branch guarantee and that Iceberg's parent_snapshot_id is cosmetically null by design. A prior produced.parent==expected assertion was REMOVED because it false-rejected every valid commit and caused the 2026-06-12 silent freeze. This is a declared position about which layer owns correctness, recorded in-code rather than derived.

A DELETE-AND-UPSERT COLLISION RESOLVES TO DELETE (:712-719). When the same key is both upserted and deleted in one batch, the upsert is dropped. That is a declared conflict rule, not a measured property of the event stream.

RETRY TUNING IS BOUNDED BY THE LAMBDA TIMEOUT, NOT BY CONVERGENCE (:41-49). COMMIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS=5, backoff cap 15s, chosen so worst-case retry wait fits inside the 180s timeout alongside derive+write. The cap is a deployment constraint presented as tuning.

key.identity_space: Two columns used as one match space: `arn` (the AWS ARN) and `node_id` (the short name). _match_filter (:391-405) builds In('arn',[...]) OR In('node_id',[...]) and the overwrite/delete filter matches a row if EITHER column hits.
key.key_expression: TWO SIDES, ONE SPACE. WRITER (lambda_function.py:701): `key = node.get('arn') or node.get('id')` -- the derived node's canonical key, the ARN when it is TRUTHY and the short id otherwise. READER, the space _match_filter actually queries (:391-405): a row matches on EITHER the `arn` column OR the `node_id` column, so a member's key is the PAIR (arn, node_id) and a consumer supplies whichever it holds. ⛔ BOTH BRANCHES OF THE `or` ARE LIVE AND THE FALLBACK IS THE MAJORITY BRANCH: at the vintage below `arn` is a non-empty ARN on 1857 of 27054 nodes and an EMPTY STRING on the other 25197, and the empty string is FALSY in Python -- so 93.1% of nodes take the `or node_id` branch. ⛔ A NULL-TEST IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT HERE AND INVERTS THE ANSWER: `arn IS NULL` is 0 of 27054, so a null-based read reports FULL ARN coverage and concludes the fallback never fires.
key.declared_mapping: delete_keys_from_event (:163-226) RECONSTRUCTS an ARN from a CloudTrail delete event's name fields, per event type, using account from recipientAccountId with fallback 313476888478 (:152) and region hardcoded us-east-1 (:153). That reconstruction IS the declared mapping between the name space and the ARN space.
key.evidence:
crosses_spaces is TRUE and measured, and the code says WHY it must: :148-151 records that CloudTrail delete events carry a NAME rather than always an ARN, and that reconstructing the ARN lets the filter match the exact node on the `arn` column 'rather than only the short name (node_id), avoiding cross-class name-collision over-delete.' So the file itself names the hazard the two-space match creates. key_is_stable='stable' is measured at the level the filter uses: an ARN is stable for a resource's lifetime and node_id is derived from it deterministically at :701 (node.get('arn') or node.get('id')). ⚠ THE STABILITY IS PER-RESOURCE, NOT ACROSS DELETE-RECREATE: an ARN reconstructed at :195 for a Lambda deleted and recreated under the same name is byte-identical, so the two incarnations are one key. Not a defect of this path -- a property of the ARN space -- but it means the key cannot distinguish resurrection from continuity. ⛔ THE REGION LITERAL IS A REAL BOUND ON THE MAPPING: _REGION='us-east-1' at :153 is hardcoded, so a delete event for a resource in any other region reconstructs an ARN that matches no row, and the delete silently no-ops. failure_mode.returns_on_failure: THREE DIFFERENT THINGS, and only one of them is loud. (1) COMMIT FAILURE: after COMMIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 CAS conflicts the handler logs ICEBERG_COMMIT_CAS_EXHAUSTED at ERROR, calls _publish_commit_failure, and RE-RAISES; the handler catches it at :735 and returns every messageId in batchItemFailures so SQS retries the whole batch. Loud and recoverable. (2) PER-RECORD FAILURE: an exception on one record logs RECORD_FAIL at ERROR and adds only that messageId to batchItemFailures (:705-707); the rest of the batch still commits. (3) ⛔ DERIVE MISS: bounded_derive_node returns None and the ARN is simply never written -- at :334 through a suppressed DEBUG line. Nothing is logged, nothing fails, the batch reports success. The commit still lands for the other ARNs and BATCH_END prints a nodes_written count that a reader will read as complete.
silent_degrade_paths: ⛔ THE PRIMARY ONE: an ARN in any of the 8 mapped-but-underived classes (cloudfront, cloudwatch, ec2, events, kms, logs, secretsmanager, states) is dropped at :334 behind a DEBUG line that :34's INFO level suppresses. The batch succeeds, failed_ids stays empty, and BATCH_END's nodes_written count is silently short. There is no signal at any level.

A live describe that throws is caught at :330 and logged BOUNDED_DERIVE_FAIL at WARNING, then returns None -- so the node is dropped, but unlike the case above it does leave a trace. This is the SAME OUTCOME reached by a LOUDER route, which is what makes the pair confusing to read in CloudWatch: two drop causes, two different volumes.

The Lambda runs in a VPC with no NAT and only S3/DynamoDB gateway endpoints (:235-237), so lambda/iam/sns/sqs describes are unroutable in-VPC and fail fast at 3s by design. Those failures land in the WARNING path above and present as ordinary derive misses rather than as a network fault.

Both SNS egress paths are documented UNROUTABLE from this VPC (:600-604, :634-640). _publish_commit_failure will therefore fail in-VPC and log COMMIT_FAILURE_SNS_FAIL at WARNING. The code names the intended real channel -- a CloudWatch Logs metric filter on the ERROR line feeding an alarm -- but that is a claim about infrastructure this card did NOT verify. I did not confirm any metric filter or alarm exists, so the loud channel is UNMEASURED at the far end.
A delete event for a resource outside us-east-1 reconstructs a non-matching ARN (:153) and the delete no-ops silently, leaving a stale node.

The marker stamp is wrapped so that its failure never fails the batch (:729-732); a commit can therefore land while the freshness marker does not advance. That is correct precedence, but it means marker staleness is not evidence the commit failed -- and the marker is the signal most readers reach for.
failure_mode.evidence: EXERCISED AS A CONTROL PAIR OVER THE LOG-LEVEL PREDICATE, both arms reachable from different truths. ARM 1 (the silent drop): :334 is logger.debug and :34 sets INFO, so the call cannot emit -- read at source, both lines quoted above. ARM 2 (POSITIVE CONTROL, same file, same function family, different truth): :256 is logger.warning for the unknown-class case and :331 is logger.warning for the describe-failure case, both of which DO emit at INFO level. So the instrument (a log line in this module) is capable of producing output, and the silence at :334 is a property of that specific call rather than of the module's logging. That is what makes distinguishable_from_true_negative='no' a measured verdict and not an assumption: a batch in which 8-class ARNs were dropped and a batch in which no such ARN arrived produce BYTE-IDENTICAL CloudWatch output. ⛔ THE CONTROL THAT MATTERS MOST IS THE ONE ON MY OWN 'IT IS LIVE' CLAIM: the branch-head marker's graph_nodes last_write_iso 2026-08-27T05:53:50.865Z is one second before its own committed_at_iso 2026-08-27T05:53:51.057095Z, and its writer_id is incremental_updater -- so the commit and the stamp are the same execution of THIS path, not a coincidence of two writers.

verdict.why: This path works and is demonstrably live: it committed to globgrph.graph_nodes 65 minutes before this carding, the deployed bytes are byte-identical to the source I read, its trigger chain is measured end to end at every hop, and its table bound is a single call-site literal that a name-keyed census finds. As the incremental writer of graph_nodes it does what it says. QUALIFIED rather than SOUND on three measured defects, all of them about what happens when it does NOT write: (1) 8 of the 14 resource classes it can classify have no derive branch and are dropped through a DEBUG line the module's own INFO level suppresses -- the drop is invisible at every log level, and the better-recognized failure is quieter than the worse-recognized one; (2) the far end of its loud channel is unverified -- both SNS paths are documented unroutable from this VPC and the CloudWatch metric-filter alarm the code names as the real channel was NOT confirmed to exist by this card; (3) the delete key space reconstructs ARNs against a hardcoded us-east-1, so an out-of-region delete no-ops silently. Not UNSOUND: nothing measured shows a wrong row being written, the CAS retry and loud re-raise are correct, and the delete-propagation design is sound. NOT INCOMPLETE: all 7 rows are worked, every scalar is 'measured', and the deployed-vs-source question is closed by content rather than by filename. ⛔ NO COMPLETENESS CLAIM ON THE WRITER POPULATION for graph_nodes, per CCY3-AC7. ⛔ NO FORWARD DISPOSITION -- omitted, and nothing here is an opinion on this path's future. Per QUALIFY-DO-NOT-FIX this lane committed nothing to this module and edited no carried surface.
